findings.result: Complete actual decision, including original review/producer metadata and source evidence, is retained with whole-decision and exact-request hashes. Finite members/SGF hashes are validated, not rewritten. Current template context/source snapshots participate in the request key. Reads reject corrupt, nonregular, symlinked or oversized records; writes use the existing atomic file pattern, private permissions and directory fsync.

Fresh identity/template/scope gates still run. Cache lookup precedes Wiki refresh and model work; hits retain original approved sources and identities, revalidate native decision/hash and current candidate/template rules. Actual complete initial or narrowed decisions are saved before later paid operations. Budget/transport errors still defer; no review is copied onto changed scope and no partial manifest is emitted.

Stage is wired as the optional decision store. Already-qualified games with empty required-name sets are grouped before paid games, before any new review has signed a scope. This does not split reviewed decisions or increase name/token/source budgets. Native publication, receiver protocol and durable paid ledger are unchanged.

Focused regression cases cover successful-review persistence before a later budget error, exact restart reuse without repaying that name, finite-scope/template change requiring a fresh review, and persistence of a completed narrowed review before a later narrowing budget error.

Cases cover restart identity preservation, changed intent misses, invalid review/membership rejection, corruption without overwrite, bounded private file handling, interrupted atomic replacement and fsync.
New focused case proves a fully reusable game is grouped before a game needing a paid name review.

limits: Producer-only incomplete calls are not approved checkpoints.
Previously lost run62158 outputs cannot be reconstructed from usage metadata by this patch.
Approval is for the pinned code, not a claim that a new deployed run or paid recovery has succeeded.
scope: Three runtime files and three scoped test files only: preserve completed finite name decisions across budget/service deferral, and group already-qualified games before paid preparation.
